answer: Retrieve the authentication token from the e2e integration’s configuration or credentials, and pass it when creating the remote iOS or Android session.

For local development, configure the e2e agent to use your personal credentials or a local authentication flow, and keep secrets out of the repository. In CI, use dedicated service credentials supplied through the CI secret store or environment variables. Avoid reusing personal credentials in CI, and ensure the CI identity has only the permissions the tests need.

Configure the iOS Expo development build’s launch arguments in e2e to point directly at the development server, and pre-grant camera access in the iOS app configuration. For example, set the Expo development-server URL in the build’s launch arguments and add `NSCameraUsageDescription` to `Info.plist`; then configure the e2e simulator/device to grant camera permission before the test runs.

Use the framework’s signed-in exploration mode to launch the app with an authenticated session, then capture screenshots through the normal screenshot API. This lets you navigate the app as a signed-in user without disabling screenshot capture.
